scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript validators for a signup form: name (required, non-empty), email (must contain @), age (must be >= 18). Run ALL validators and return ALL errors at once, not just the first one.
criteria: Uses Validate (not Either) so errors accumulate instead of short-circuiting
Merges the results of the validators with .combine() or sequenceValidate
Returns all errors, not just the first one that fails

scenarios.prompt: Write a DTO validator for CreateProductDto: name (non-empty string), price (positive number), stock (non-negative integer). Each validator should return a typed FieldError object with a field name and message. Accumulate ALL errors.
criteria: Uses Validate.valid() and Validate.invalid() (or the equivalent valid()/invalid() functions) with typed error objects
Error type includes a field name (not just a plain string)
Uses .combine() or sequenceValidate to collect all errors from all fields

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: validate an array of numbers where each must be positive and less than 1000. Return ALL numbers that fail with their index and reason. Use sequenceValidate.
criteria: Uses sequenceValidate to validate all items
Does not short-circuit: all items are validated even after the first failure
Returns errors from all failing items, not just the first

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: existing validators return Validate<string, T> with messages formatted as 'field: reason' (e.g. 'email: must contain @'). For a CreateAccount request (email, password, age), run all the validators and accumulate every error. The HTTP layer needs FieldError objects { field, message } instead of strings. Return { status: 201, body: account } when valid, or { status: 422, body: FieldError[] } listing every error.
criteria: Converts each string error into a FieldError with .mapInvalid() on the Validate, instead of unwrapInvalid().map(...) inside an isInvalid() branch
Builds both responses with a single .match() on the combined Validate (no isValid()/unwrap() branching)
Accumulates the errors of all fields with .combine() or sequenceValidate

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: a profile form has username (required, 3-20 chars) and displayName (optional). validateDisplayName(s) returns Validate<string, string> and fails with 'displayName: empty' for an empty value or with other messages such as 'displayName: too long'. When the only problem is that displayName is empty, use the username as the display name instead of failing; any other displayName errors must still be reported. All errors of all fields must be returned together.
criteria: Uses .bindInvalid() on the displayName Validate to inspect the whole error list and recover with a valid value when the only error is 'empty'
Keeps the other displayName errors invalid (returns the errors from bindInvalid, or does not recover) instead of dropping them
Combines the username and displayName results with .combine() (or sequenceValidate) so errors from both fields are reported together

scenarios.prompt: Express + Prisma signup route. Validate email and password synchronously, and check that the email is not already taken with an async isEmailTaken(email): Promise<boolean>; report all problems together. When everything is valid, save the user with prisma.user.create(...) and respond 201 with the user; otherwise respond 422 with the list of errors.
criteria: Accumulates the async uniqueness error with the sync errors, via .combineAsync()/sequenceValidateAsync or by awaiting the check and merging its Validate with .combine()/sequenceValidate
Uses .matchAsync() with an async valid handler that saves the user, and an invalid handler that builds the 422 response
Does not branch on isValid()/isInvalid() or call unwrap()/unwrapInvalid() to build the responses
